I am not the only one with this problem. YouTubers Sailing Magic Carpet recently reported the same exact issue that we have observed. The overall quality of Navionics map data is good but the quality of the app itself is unacceptable.

title: How does one spell money grab? G-A-R-M-I-N
body: In response to the Developer reply, I’m aware of that, and you obviously didn’t comprehend the issue at all. If someone has already paid a lot of $$$ for your product (in this case the 943xsv AND a subscription to Navionics+ for said chartplotter) a company that cares about its customers should offer a discount if one wants to supplement with another Navionics subscription for a phone/tablet. Having to pay full price for both is a sleazy tactic. It’s not a difficult concept to comprehend.) My original review still applies a year later. Despite having the exact same chart info on my Garmin GPSMap 943xsv, I’m forced to pay twice for the info - once for this subscription, and a separate price for the 943xsv subscription. How Garmin has not made a discounted bundle available for loyal customers is absurd. That a premium subscription to this mobile app isn’t included with a Navionics+ charplotter subscription, that was also purchased from Garmin, is insulting. Not to mention the asinine decision to allow only TWO devices to access the charts at a time. Why? Does Garmin really think this program is being shared like Netflix? So when we’re cruising and plotting in real time, if we want the iPad to always have the information available, one of us has to sign out of Navionics on our iPhones.

title: So much worse than it should be

Other minor complaints: The relief shading is great, but it’s not used to report depth, so depths are often extremely inaccurate, even in areas with high resolution relief shading. The app is a battery hog.

title: Frustrated with Navionics Boating
body: I am so angry with Navionics that it is hard to know where to start. I have been a heavy user of the Navionics Boating app since 2015 while sailing from Australia to the Mediterranean. With the problems in the updated app and cost to buy the charts for three regions twice to have them on the two phones and two iPads that my husband and I will use on our 36-foot sailboat during our upcoming passage from Malta to the Caribbean, we are ready to ditch the app and start over with another. Here’s the problems I found yesterday after updating the app and subscribing to three chart areas we will need. I am pretty sure there are more problems that are not yet obvious to me. Night vision is horrible because the dark color on the water obscures important chart data such as depths and hazards!!! Can this feature be disabled? It turns on automatically at night. I selected day view, but am not confident the problem won’t recur automatically at a critical moment in the future. Switching back to North Up every time you touch the screen is frustrating and potentially dangerous. The chart orientation should stay the way the mariner sets it until they change the setting. Changing the chart orientation without warning is dangerous. I read that you can prevent the problem by just using the plus and minus arrows to zoom in and out which are a very crude way to do so. It is a touch screen so the touch features should be usable without altering the chart orientation. All of the views except chart view may be dangerous because they obscure navigation data such as depth! The nautical chart data should be clearly presented no matter what overlay is added. It is a boating navigation app after all. I have always been annoyed at Navionics for ignorantly calling nautical charts maps. The latest updates clearly confirms my long time suspicion that the developers are not mariners, have no regard for safety at sea, and develop features just because they think they would be technically cool. They should try using features they develop to actually navigate a vessel at sea before adding them to the app. What might seem like a great feature while sitting at a desk in an office could be a disaster at sea. Is anybody actually a mariner at Navionics? Do they ever ask mariners what they want? Do they test prospective new features on an actual boat before adding them to the app? Anyway, the above are the list of defects we have discovered on our updated Navionics Boating app in less than 24 hours. There are probably more serious gotchas that we don’t want to discover on our passage from the Mediterranean to the Caribbean later this year. Yesterday we renewed our Boating Navionics chart area subscription for the Med and added Africa and the Caribbean before using the updated app. We are very unhappy with the app changes and regard some as outright dangerous. Since we bought the charts we should be able to use them in any app, we prefer one created by more responsible developers. I will ask but doubt a refund or transfer will be accommodated. After I ran into problems with Navionics Boating in the last 24 hours I decided to read through the reviews in the Apple App Store. I discovered that I am not the only one having these problems. I also saw clearly that there is no real and effective effort by the developers to help their customers and fix the serious problems they reported. I even found myself wondering if the responses to reviews are AI generated without any human being from Boating Navionics involved. We are retired pensioners on a fixed and modest income. The limit of having Navionics Boating charts on only two devices is unacceptable on our 36-foot sailboat with a crew of two. That expense is in addition to buying the charts from Navionics for our two RayMarine chartplotters. We have two iPhones and two iPads. We tried my husband logging out of his iPhone and me logging into the app on our iPad. No joy. The charts disappeared and required being downloaded again! To get Navionics operational again on my iPad I would have to buy the charts again for an additional $150!!!!! We should be able to use our expensive Navionics Boating charts on all of our devices. I read that Aqua Maps allows theirs to be used on five devices per subscription. Navionics has now started requiring logging into an account to start the app if you have been logged out. The process requires 2-part authentication via a numeric code sent to your email address. It is clear that Navionics does not understand that boats are often in places without an Internet connection. Imagine getting inadvertently logged out of Navionics in the middle of an ocean passage and needing a code from an email address you don’t have access to offshore to bring your navigation system back up!!! I wrote this review without any expectation of a satisfactory response from the company. I wanted to give other mariners a heads up to the problems we have experienced in just a few days. Others might benefit from knowing before they decide which navigation app and charts to purchase for their boat.

title: Would not recommend. Not even basic free function. Read my description
body: Unless you plan on being a yearly paid subscriber, this app is not for you. I just downloaded it and the first screen that pops up is telling me my Trial expired and click here to subscribe. Uhh, ok no. I clicked no thanks wanting to see what it’s all about. It forces me to Garmin’s page to create an account first and agree to all of their terms of use and privacy policies…*grumble grumble*.. I just wanna see how it works. I read through pages and pages of terms and policies, linking to other pages of terms and policies, and linking to policies for their affiliates with whom you are also agreeing to… Then it finally lets me in to the most 8-bit NES inaccurate map ever and starts popping up windows saying BUY MAPS. Clear it. BUY MAPS!. Clear it….*grumble grumble* I go to the layers function to see what layers I can turn on… all the overlays pop up a screen saying subscribe. The 3 layers on top, 2 of them say subscribe when selected, and the one saying “nautical maps”, which looks like the basic type of map that would be provided free by NOAA (go to NOAA’s site for free charts btw), lets you select it and close the window, but never applies it. So unless you’re paying $150/year, this app is useless. Don’t waste your time consenting to Garmin having your private information. Yet another thing Garmin ruins with their greed. Garmin offers amazing premium services, but there should be a PRO version for that. And let me use the basic for free so I can want the premium stuff and switch. There are tons of useful free nautical navigation apps out there that give you basic features to move around. Like “saavy navvy”, and it works right out of the box for free. Don’t bother replying developers, not interested. I’m deleting my app and the account right after this.

title: Doesn’t work

title: You lost me!
body: I have subscribed to this app for years, even when you increased the price and forced Canada on us i still stayed! But you have now lost me, i refuse to pay $50 a year for an app that i spend all day proving wrong! Shading does not work properly and depths and contours are all wrong on my local lakes. App says humps and vex proves there is nothing there. Get the livescope out to verify and further prove that the app is no where near close to accurate! title: Price hike is ridiculous

title: Distracting and unsafe
body: The inability to lock the map view in the course up or heads up mode is absolutely unacceptable and dangerous. Every time you pan or zoom the map, the map view resets. In order to get a desired map view back, you need to touch a very small icon twice while on a fast moving vessel. This app behavior is extremely distracting, frustrating and unsafe! Furthermore, the map doesn't pan automatically as the vessel moves; you have to pan it manually, which results in the map view being reset repeatedly. I recommend the folks designing this app to try to actually use it on a fast moving vessel as that would help them understand how dysfunctional this app actually is.

title: Worth 10 stars before update now 1

Without subscribing, there are no depths, channel markers or even detailed land areas. The subscription costs $25!!! Worst app ever!

title: Getting worse every month.
body: This was a fantastic app 10 years ago. As the industry has shrunk to very few players/no competition it is now lousy. Basically, you should remain at all times in a strong WiFi environment at all times to get the most of it. It is possible to go boating short distances if you do not stray out of cell range. But going over the horizon - forget it! Their insane catchphrase, “We start where the road ends”. Should be, “Reach the horizon & you are LOST.” I’ve sailed From Hobart to Darwin in the past 4 months - usually without knowing exactly where I am. Very frustration and literally HUNDREDS of messages between a Navionics Bot & I. There may not be any humans working at Navionics except in the billing department. I have bought & downloaded C-maps also crap. And bought a Navionics card of Australia which seems to make my Brad new plotter fight with the app on my phone & tablet. In 2009 I made a 1600Nm voyage with my iPhone 3 and Navionics app - flawless! The good old days!

title: Functionality and cost.
body: Previously loved the APP and NAVIONICS…. I’m trying to figure out after buying $160 Navionics + Card and an app that has nearly doubled in price to include regions I will never use in Alaska and Canada, why I need to pay another $140 for the + just to keep the functionality between the app and my chart plotter to communicate? I know that in a previous review support mentioned the increase in cost of maps and data. I have already purchased these. An increase of the cost of the app is totally understandable. Being charged $140 just to sync routes between the plotter should not constitute the purchase price of the original card especially when those routes and data can be shared for free between other APP users (In theory). In addition users who sync their bathymetry using live sonar which is taken and uploaded for Navionics use and sales all why using using our equipment. I understand the model, however it hardly seems equitable. Finally, if both the app and card and plotter synchronization worked flawlessly I would have a little to say but, the only time my app sees my NAVIONICS + card it’s a notify me that my subscription is expired and then I can renew. So I did and that was the last time they talked. Beyond that I am unable to sync routes, waypoints or any other data reliably or dependably and take the most time in preparation for a trip. Over $300 invested in the app/card/update seems pretty ridiculous for what is promised and what actually is delivered. I have read countless articles on the Raymarine and Navionics sites before posting here and none of them provide any useful insight, detail or troubleshooting. No live support period. I sent an email to tech support at Navionics and am awaiting a reply I will update my review with the outcome.

I opened my app to use it only to find that I needed to pay to use it AGAIN! Every other app developer grandfathers their current customers who helped support them. Not Navionics! Make sure you know that at any time Navionics may decide that they want to make more money off of you and when they do, they’ll simply stop providing what you paid for and demand more money to use the product you already bought. Buyer beware!!! Note the response from Navionics. I can re-download the app I already bought. They replaced my purchased app with the subscription app hoping I’d just roll over and pay again! Deal with this unscrupulous amoral company at your own risk.

title: Stops updating while underway
body: I really like this navigation App for the dock to dock routing and ETA using my IPhone in addition to my MFD. Unfortunately, it stops updating randomly after a few minutes which isn’t always obvious (not what you need when you’re underway and in unfamiliar waters with a lot of boat traffic. I reported this problem last year and figured they would have fixed it by now since it is a serious issue. Unfortunately not. I upgraded my iphone from a SE3 to a new 16e but have the same problem with no difference. It’s hard to believe that a $50 annual subscription doesn’t buy better software support from a major company such as Garmin. In 2026, the problem still has not been resolved. I have determined that the problem is with a SW graphing routine getting hung. Evidence of this is that the program doesn’t hang on IOS if it is running in the background. If it is running in the foreground, it will randomly hang during map graphing update. Garmin says it is a problem with Apple GPS not registering a change due to slow velocity (6 kts is not slow). I can see how this could be a lawsuit against Garmin since they have not resolved a serious problem that could cause a boat navigation disaster. For $50/yr, I expect that this serious problem working with IOS would be resolved. Good thing Garmin has plenty of money for a future lawsuit.

title: Chart gerrymandering

For example, the ABC islands which are in the Caribbean are now excluded from the Caribbean chart on my plotter, but used to be there when I visited in 2014 and 2016. Also, the Mediterranean chart covers Gibraltar but omits Morocco. Sailing from Gibraltar to Las Palmas will require the user to purchase the African continent to be converted for 40 miles along the Moroccan coastline. Sailing the Caribbean will require the purchase of South America is you want to visit the ABC islands. Is this corporate oversight or greed?

title: Beware New Sign-In Requirement
body: Update: First, I appreciate the diligent attention of Garmin representatives to the reviews and the prompt responses. That is the kind of behavior that over the years we have come to expect from Garmin. But, in the case of this app, I am afraid that the response is a bit Kafkaesque. Some years ago I bought (not rented or subscribed to) the Navionics app and base maps for lifetime use. In recent years, following Garmin’s acquisition of Navionics, the app was replaced with a new app (with purchased maps carried over). Now we are told that we must pay “rent” (a subscription) for things that we previously have owned outright. And to enforce Garmin’s desire to have us pay rent, we are threatened with the app being disabled if we do not “upgrade” to a version that facilitates Garmin’s enforcement of newly collecting “rent” on these things already owned. One guesses that somewhere in hundreds/thousands of pages of terms and conditions (unfathomable to anyone, including lawyers) Garmin believes that it has granted itself permission to newly collect rent on things already owned. But isn’t that really beneath Garmin? I own several Gramin products and have used various Garmin services over the years and this does not seem to be in the character of the company that I know. With around a billion dollars in annual net income, is Garmin so in need of cash that it wishes to tarnish its reputation with such antics? This seems to be a “penny wise; pound foolish” moment, but you decide. I bought Navionics years ago because I would own (rather than subscribe) to the maps and because the app worked entirely offline. In those respects it has been great and I have been quite happy with it. But with an app update a few months back Garmin created a potentially life-threatening situation by locking the app until one signs into a Garmin account online. I was on a trip, out of cellular range, started the app and it would do nothing except demand signing in, which was not possible because I had no Internet connection. Fortunately I had another navigation alternative. But for anyone that wouldn’t have another navigation source the situation could turn grim very fast. I am quite disappointed that Garmin would create such a risk for the evident reason of collecting personally-identifiable data for marketing. You are the product, apparently even if it means a risk to safety. I will avoid any further updates to this app, which worked fine until the marketing department got involved.

We had to delete the app and reinstall (and we were lucky enough to discover the issue while in port in order to re-download it). I would recommend not updating the app to 14.1 (or at least not deleting charts) if you rely on this app until a future update with some better error checking/bug fixing comes our way. Thank you for the continued development in our favorite charting app! ————————————————— Original review March 2019 Wonderful app! You can’t beat the price and accuracy of the charts. We plan to use this app to circumnavigate over the next two years. East coast of USA, Bahamas, and Panama have all been wonderful and accurate so far. I am able to install the app on backup cellular data iPads in lifeproof cases. We use this app as our chart plotter. One of the bugs we have noticed seems to relate to low internet speed. title: Be careful with depths in SonarChart mode
body: In the SonarChart mode, the app was reporting about a 25 foot water depth between a small island and the nearby shoreline. As I started to across the area, my depth sounder showed me in less than 10 feet of water. I toggled over to Navigation Chart mode, and the same spot that showed 25 feet of water now showed as about 10 feet of water in the app. But then my depth finder reported maybe 6 feet of water. Then I realized another important flaw in the app. It does not factor in the water level offset when displaying the water depth when you touch a spot on the map. So while it showed about 10 feet when I touched the map in the questionable area, it should have displayed about a 5 foot depth due to my -5 water level correction. Ironically, the nearby contour lines do factor in the lake level ( the water level offset), but not the crosshair lines that appear when you touch a spot on the chart. I have all the latest chart updates in this app. I also run a pair of Garmin 1243xsv units on my main boat with the very latest Navionics Vision+ charts for the eastern and southern USA waters, and they exhibited the same problem when toggling from a fishing chart to the navigation chart. I turned on community contours to see if those overlays would fix the incorrect water depth, but no community contours appeared for the spot in question. I understand things can be off by a foot or two, but keep in mind the water depth that I ran through was about 20 feet less than what the SonarChart map in the app and my chart plotters were showing. I reported the area to Garmin, but the moral of this story is don’t fully trust these things to give you completely accurate data no matter what you pay and how many times a week you update your charts. all that said, I found the mobile phone app to be very helpful when navigating at night on a smaller ski boat. The auto guidance really helps you find the channel markers and go around them versus running through them when there’s not much moonlight. Like many others here, I’ve been happily paying up to about 20 bucks a year to keep an active subscription, but I think this may be my last year. $50 per year is pretty high for something I might use 6 times a year for night rides on the lake. If you own Garmin chartplotters, you have similar functionality in the Chart mode of the ActiveCaptain app. I don’t think the ActiveCaptain Chart user interface is quite as nice as the Navionics Boating app, but it will suffice when occasionally navigating on a rental boat or my smallest boat that lacks a chartplotter. I hope Garmin reconsiders the annual subscription fee and comes up with some options like just the Eastern USA for $25 or just the Southeast USA for 20 bucks.

body: I like the app but it crashes frequently. Like about every other time I launch it or so, it crashes and I have to reboot it.

title: Good app somewhat glitchy
body: Mostly good lately I can not adjust depth shading. I set it to where I want and it just reverts back to 30’

title: Needs inshore/offshore option
body: It is a great app for our business, however it needs inshore and offshore options.

title: 3 wishing 4 more
body: To be honest, I love this app. Would I give it more than 3 stars? No. I use it a lot and it has some problems. Yes, could partly be my cell phone- regarding tracking. However, it’d be nice if they would dial things in the slow speed accuracy (drifting) realm. I tend to have to restart the app to get it to update location when Im drifting. Seems to lock up when I stop motoring to drift And, it doesn’t point to the direction Im drifting. Constantly bounces the arrow around. On the ocean, it’s not always easy to determine where you’re drifting. That being said, Im not giving the app up. However, it’s 2026. Somebody’s gonna bring things to the market. Ill stay here if they don’t get beat.

title: Not a bad app
body: Everything is good, I just wish precious saved trails can be selected to stay on. If I go out one day and save my trail, the next day I cannot follow it. It saves it and I can see it,(However recently the screen goes all grey when studying it) but cannot follow old trails while underway making new trails.

title: Still the top boating app
body: It’s the best pocket app for boating or quickly making a bathy chart, some things could use a little polishing however

title: Great app… power drain
body: I use this app all the time on the water, my only complaint is how fast it deteriorates battery. I have an iPhone 15 max, I only get a few hours on the water because it eats it so fast. Fix this, and it’s the best.

title: App is great but might be getting hacked
body: The APP is wonderful. On or off the lakes the track works. The lake contours are perfect. The APP is worth the $50 per year. But——Ever since I order the US lakes, I have been getting second verification texts. Several a day. I reset my password but the app is going nuts or someone is trying to access my maps. I tried to email the support center but they keep sending to another Garmin division. I would think a security issue would trigger a positive replay from any Garmin group.

title: Change of Priorities
body: It is clear that this apps priority has changed. It seems to set a priority on making sure you have selected the correct tide station to the detriment of assisting a boater guide their boat. This is still a great app, but this feature is dumb.

title: Tides
body: Recently used this app on a trial basis and was great for the water ways I was working showed me exact tides n times ! Easily , will subscribe after trial ends

title: Make Apple Watch compatible
body: What would make this app top tier is if compatible to watch and you could easy read depth that would be sweet

title: Cost
body: Best charts so far but has got too expensive now now looking for different app unless prices change not sure why they went up

title: Works well but tough to use on cell phone
body: I’ve got the large pro max iPhone but it’s still very tough to see and read while boating… no fault of the app. The only thing that is a real pain is having to re-hit the location arrow to reset it to track your motion, after every time you touch the map for any other reason. Have only used the trial for a few days so I’m not totally familiar with it. I do think it would be an excellent backup but I think I need a much larger screen.

title: Amazing app but needs monthly subscription
body: I really love this app I’ve used it so many times going out kayaking on the lake. However the only call back to it is that you have to pay $50 yearly and unfortunately I don’t even fish most of the winter months so it would be nice if they could add in monthly subscription.

title: My opinion
body: Thanks for app , but i think it needs to some tools , such as a circle , square , line and … , and sometimes it not connect to gps Thank you

title: New limit on device logins
body: I’ve been using Navionics for a little over 5 years and it’s my go to charting software along side my Garmin chart plotter. As full time cruisers, my wife and I use it, often simultaneously, to find and route destinations. Between us we have 4 devices, 2 phones and 2 iPads. One of the recent updates now limits the number of devices logins per account to 2. Unfortunately this was not stated in the customer facing change logs. Now we are often faced with “too many devices logged in” and must choose which to disconnect. I understand the need to limit logins to prevent people from sharing the account outside of their family, but only 2 devices is too tight. Give us 4!

title: Great app, but could use a few things
body: I love the app for many reasons, the shading feature is great for finding new spots, you can save tracks and spots and use them offline. The app is great in many ways but you can only have 1000 markers, which is a lot, but I should be able to have as many markers as my storage allows for; not an arbitrary cap. As far as the shading goes I would like more scanned bottom in my area. Aside from those two things I think the app is great. Please let me have more markers in your next update.

title: Great, missing key data for Hawaii
body: Great app, planning on using it more for diving. Just wondering why current data isn’t available in Hawaii? Thank you!

title: Love it, but fails on some iPads at low speeds
body: Navionics is my primary chart plotter on my sailboat. I absolutely love it except for one bug. On some iPads it does not work below 5 knots. I need to use my android phone when going slowly while leaving and entering harbors. This is also when it is most critical. I use it minor percent of the time when at speed. Route planning is absolutely amazing. it is nearly a matter of clicking on the start and end points on the chart. Maybe add an interesting point or two if you have specific route changes that you like. In 30 seconds, I can now plan what used to make me hours with paper.

title: Great app but needs location update fix
body: So fantastic must have app but sometimes with latest version when opening or switching back to app it will show a stale boat location with no indicator that it’s stale and it just doesn’t update until u force kill and re launch. You CANNOT show stale location especially with no indicator that it’s old. Can be dangerous. Get this fixed ASAP please.

title: Good navigation
body: I like the app though on IOS screen times out very quickly making it difficult to continuously navigate. Also, uses way more better than google maps…

title: Track Editing
body: Would be helpful if there was a way to edit saved track length.

title: Love this app but hard to get any tech support
body: This app is super useful as a fisherman mariner in Alaska but it was annoying that I bought the AIS overlay for 100$ and it doesn’t work where I live in Alaska because there are no receivers up here where I live. Can’t figure out how or where to request a refund. Would appreciate some guidance if someone from the company is reading this.

title: Life saver
body: Ok. Formerly a 1 star. Frustrated it always said unable to calculate route. However after working with navionics (great customer care) we figured out it was the boat settings. It now works beautifully Boat with confidence! Wish it wouldn’t change orientation when touching the map. Would love it to stay on course up. Thanks for the help navionics!!

title: Lame
body: Bought this app and now they want me to pay a subscription for it? Old one is basically worthless, as they’re ant to force us to pay monthly for it. So lame.

title: Need to Remove Thunderforest popup
body: Thank you, for the help on how to remove “Thunderforest popup” by changing overlays.

title: Help!
body: This app is excellent and really gives the detail that is needed! …

title: Love it. Important update info
body: The new changes to the auto-route function caused problems to me. It is no longer able to calculate some simple routes if they are long, and adds turns/indirect courses even when a direct line is shorter (and free of hazards). I asked them to please bring back the old auto-routing algorithms! They replied with the following helpful advice: “ Please try to download and update the charts going in Menu>>Download Maps. Try again to calculate the Route. Please check also if crossing the bridges on the base of the height in your Boat Settings. For long distances, we suggest to add an intermediate waypoint.” The last piece of adding an additional waypoint worked well for me. Solved my problem. (Thanks) This is a full featured and very capable program that is among the best. (Edited to add additional info)

title: Doesn’t work.
body: So. I paid my $24.99 for this app. Whenever you try and ‘boat to’ anywhere it just pops up an error about the map downloading. Even though the map is downloaded. Great way to throw money down the drain. Edit. A couple of extra stars added as it did work eventually but the autoroute feature which I bought the subscription for sends a boat with a 2 foot draft through areas that are a few inches deep at low tide. Seems a little flaky still

title: Issue with GPS data
body: The app is getting depth and AIS from SignalK server, but the GPS data over NMEA 0183 via Wifi on my iPad without an internal GPS chip is not working. I verified with OpenCPN that the SignalK is working properly. Please fix.

title: I use it to navigate a 100 ton vessel
body: Honestly this thing is great, especially for fishing. The only request I have is for it to support split screen multitasking, then it’ll be a 5 star app

title: Rock Solid!!!
body: I have used Navionics for years. Could you change the pins (distance and bearing) to meters, matching the depth?

title: Amazing up but needs a special update
body: Please update the app for iPhone duo users this would be a huge update and would help a lot of users out and the app would look amazing.

title: Excellent Plotter Primary or Backup
body: Using for 2 seasons now in Puget Sounds and Canadian areas. Extremely accurate charts with superb detail. Depths are accurate and hazards well marked. Some coves and anchorages a bit conservative. Automatic course plotting is convenient and reliable. I use it alongside my Furuno Navnet for independent course verification. Excellent for advance trip planning.

title: Inland lakes
body: I stay off the ocean but this app has been fantastic for me on unfamiliar lakes. Has never let me down even with no cell service. Just download the maps before you head out

title: great app
body: this app is definitely worth i. gets me through the channel and is pretty simple to use

title: Inland Waters the best
body: Exceeded my expectations and it just keeps getting better. I’ve yet to boat an inland lake of river that Navionics has not mapped.

title: Great Navigation App.
body: I am a fisherman and pleasure boater on KY & Barkley Lake. Garmin is what I use on the fishing boat and I bow loaded it for my phone for my pleasure boat. It is 10X better than the Lowrance for its contours and bottom mapping. I wanted a good app for my phone so I didn’t have to mount a graph onto my pleasure boat. I would definitely buy this app any day of the week for spending time on the water.

title: Laguna Madre approval
body: I can’t believe this app doesn’t have higher ratings. I use it to navigate around the Upper Laguna Madre and it hasn’t failed me. I have personal areas marked for “no go” spots and it gets me through the Narrow cuts that I need for my boats draft. 5⭐️

title: I cant add Maldives charts
body: Pls help me

title: Great for my skiff in coastal creeks
body: I did the trial periods on all the main boating navigation apps and finally settled on this one and paid for the one year subscription. The detailed contours of the coastal creeks near me are by far the best. I can confidently cruise around without running aground. Phone is on a suction cup mount with a battery charger, stays on for hours without issue. Tracks, auto routes, shows tides, wind, weather. Great app. Don’t understand the bad reviews, it’s better than the other apps for me. Includes coastal and inland all in one.

title: Really good nav app
body: I don't know how this is not rated higher, relief shading is excellent auto routing is excellent, I prefer this over any other app for backup to my Garmin units. Works great offshore and inshore.

title: MeckPomm Seenplatte super
body: War sehr beeindruckt von der Qualität u Detailtreue der Karten. Einfache Bedienung. Absolut zuverlässige Navigation auf einem iPad Pro. Am besten fand ich den Offline Download der Karten, so dass während des Törns kein Internet notwendig ist. Super!

title: Great app, needs magnetic north
body: This is an excellent navigation app, but the fact that bearings use true north instead of magnetic north makes it essentially unusable for sail boat racers. Adding the correction mentally each time makes it very hard to think through multiple sailing angles at once.

title: My go to app
body: I have thousands of dollars of charting information on my boat but this is my go to application. It also works on multiple boats and cruise ships.

title: Finally Back To The Future
body: I’ve gone through the extreme machinations of this app. It used to be great. Then it was modified so that the route plots adhered to buoys which resulted in a tortured route which was extremely difficult to straighten out. Then, suddenly, the routes did not download to my Simrad chart plotter and I had to transfer the routes manually through my computer. Finally, the app now works like it used to. The routes transfer effortlessly and the route plots are much better. The only problem is I’m now faced with the question of whether to download the latest update. Did they screw up again or is the modification an improvement? Who knows?

title: Nice to have
body: V very good 👍
What is the renewal price? Please forward to me , I would like to know what you are going to charge.

title: Offset
body: Love this app. I did the entire great-loop using my iPad as primary navigation with this app. One comment… when using “course up” or whatever orientation as my preference, there should be an option for the vessel to be offset 2/3 so that the charted area ahead of me dominates the display. I think the only option now is to be centered. But I just don’t care about seeing all the chart area behind me. 2/3 offset should be a display option. Thank you!

title: Lost
body: I logged out on accident and I can’t remember what email I used. Anyway to find it?

title: Indispensable
body: In my opinion it’s as indispensable as a cb radio if you are going off shore fishing way more valuable than it’s price 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

title: Great app!
body: I have been using navionics for 8 years, user friendly. One nice to have would be the ability to add notes to markers. I love dropping a pin everywhere we anchor but would like to leave more information regarding swell, what to look out for, etc.

title: Great app for serious trip planning and backup
body: I have use this app for at least 5 years. It’s east to use and amazing. I have used it from FL up the Tenn Tom and all over the Great Lakes. I don’t understand the negative reviews. Even when I am underway I will have this running on my phone or on the iPad.

title: App not working
body: Love the app. Have had it for several years now. Only problem is now it won’t open. Just did the new update hoping that would fix my issue but still nothing.

title: Good
body: Best app for marine

title: Crashing more
body: 8/24/22 - Have been using this app since they got rid of the location specific versions. Was very stable but has recently degraded. This season it will only be open for a few seconds to maybe a minute then crashes. Not good if try to use for navigation. Phone is only 2 years old so would be surprised by compatibility issues this soon. If this keeps up and is still present next spring will need to use another charting app. 8/26/22 - Update: customer service is responsive and helped solve the issue. The app is functioning normally again

title: Best app ever.
body: I am a master Captian. I use this app religiously. On my own boat I never turn on the Chartplotter. I use Navionics on my iPad. When I do a delivery I do the same. The auto guidance is amazing as is the sonar charts. I’ve traveled from Dubuque Iowa to Jacksonville Florida using this app on an iPad and never had a problem. It’s just great.

title: Long press navigation not working
body: Overall much better than my older raymarine.

title: Long time user. First time reviewer
body: The Navionics app has always been a good backup to my chart plotter but the dock to dock routing has been lack luster. However, I just tried it again and it is massively improved. It’s now useful when plotting a cruise up and down the ICW. Thanks Navionics dev team!
